To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the slow component of tau transport is not affected by the presence of the EGFP tag, by the N-terminal inserts, by the C-terminal repeat, or by the presence of mutations in the tau protein.

1) the slow transport rate of tau isoforms is not significantly affected by the presence of N-terminal inserts or the C-terminal repeats, and 2) the slow transport of mutant tau isoforms is unaffected by missense mutations in the protein.
the microtubuie-associated protein tau is transported along axon with a speed of ~ 2 mm/day and that mutations in the protein do not significantly affect the transport rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transport of microtubule-binding proteins along neuronal axons.
understanding the molecular mechanism that underlies the slow transport of tau and the role of different isoforms and mutants in this process.
the axonal transport of the microtubular protein tau.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the slow axonal transport rate of tau is not affected by the presence of the EGFP tag, the presence of either three or four repeats, the presence of two N-terminal inserts, or by the presence of missense mutations.
the slow axonal transport rate of tau is not a significant factor in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease.
the exon 1 N-terminal inserts and the exon 10-encoded C-terminal repeats of the microtubules-associated protein tau have no significant regulatory role in slow axonal transport.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the slow axonal transport rates of different tau isoforms and mutants are not significantly different from one another, suggesting that the slow axon transport rate is not a significant factor in the pathophysiology of tau-mediated neurodegeneration.

we have developed a methodology for measuring the transport of different tau isoforms and mutants in cultured neurons and that we found that neither the C-terminal repeat nor N-terminal inserts of tau, nor missense mutations, affect the rate of transport.

the microtuble-associated protein tau is transported along axon with a speed comparable to that previously measured in vivo and that mutations that are associated with neurodegeneration do not affect the slow transport of tau.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the slow transport rates of tau and other axonal cargoes can be measured in cultured neurons and that the methodology is robust, sensitive, and quantitative.

the methodology we have developed enables the transport characteristics of individual isoforms and mutants of the microtubul-associated protein tau to be measured, and we demonstrate the lack of effect of either the C-terminal repeats or the N-terminal insert domains on the rate of slow axonal transport.

the methodology developed here can be used to study transport characteristics of a large number of tau isoforms and mutants, which may provide insight into the mechanism underlying neurodegenerative diseases.
